draft.title: Hypothetical Memory Usage for LLM Context Lengths: 2048 vs 8192 (Fixed Hardware)
draft.body:
This post discusses a hypothetical experiment exploring the memory footprint of different context lengths in local language models. In this theoretical scenario, we consider a fixed model, runtime, and hardware setup. The primary focus is on the RAM consumption associated with scaling context. 

For a hypothetical context length of 2048 tokens, the estimated memory usage was 7 GB. When scaling this up to a context length of 8192 tokens, the hypothetical memory usage increased to 11 GB. It's important to reiterate that these are hypothetical figures from a planned experiment, not measured results. No output quality or throughput benchmarks were collected as part of this hypothetical setup. The goal was solely to observe the direct memory overhead introduced by longer contexts under controlled, theoretical conditions. Further investigation into performance implications would require actual testing.

The objective is to quantify the theoretical RAM increase when dealing with larger input sequences.

According to the hypothetical test parameters, a context length of 2048 tokens was associated with approximately 7 GB of RAM usage.
